the effect of a change in the diet on the animal performances during an established infection with GIN.
the effects of the nutritional status on gastrointestinal nematode infection and its consequences on the host's performances.
the effect of changes to the nutritional status on animal performances and the control of GIN infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the improvement of animal performance by the use of protein supplements in a GIN infected animal is at the expense of a higher parasite load and that the use of protein supplement should not be recommended in the context of a GIN endemic area.

, in the context of this experimental study, the improvement of the nutritional status of Creole kids during a GIN infection would be beneficial to their performance at the expense (at least partially) of the mechanism involved to control the infection.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nutritional status of growing kids is an important factor in the control of GIN infection and should be considered in the design of control programs.
a better nutritional status during an established infection would improve animal performance but at the expense of a better control of the infection.

the improvement of nutritional status during the establishment of an experimental GIN infection would increase animal performance but together with an increase of the intensity and severity of infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better nutritional status during an established GIN infection would increase the animal performance at a slight but significant cost for the control of the GIN infections.
the nutritional status of growing Creole animals should not be neglected in order to maintain their growth performances during GIN infection.
the improvement of animal performances during a GIN infection could have a cost in terms of the intensity of infection and the need for a better understanding of the mechanism involved.
